questions.title: Which candidate will receive the most “encourage” votes in the first UN Security Council straw poll of the 2026 secretary-general selection?
questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.

(2) Macky Sall trims 0.07 -> 0.05 after Ugandan former UN USG Olara Otunnu formally entered on July 24-26 as the 7th candidate, breaking Sall's solo-African status (partially offset by Gabon President Oligui Nguema's July 25 unity endorsement) and widening residual for Espinosa + Otunnu from 0.02 to 0.03. local_articles.title: UN to hold informal polls for new UN chief from Thursday
local_articles.snippet: July 28 - The United Nations Security Council will hold an initial round of informal closed-door "straw poll" ballots on Thursday to assess support for the seven candidates currently vying to become the next head of the United Nations. The candidates, from Argentina, Chile, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guyana, Senegal and Uganda, are seeking to replace Antonio Guterres of Portugal when he steps down at the end of this year after two five-year terms. Guterres' successor faces the task of revitalizing an organization in crisis and declining stature that is under increasing pressure to reform a bloated, costly bureaucracy and cut duplication across its many agencies. Straw polls are informal, non-binding votes conducted among the Security Council's 15 members. They are asked whether they "encourage," "discourage" or have "no opinion" on each candidate. local_articles.title: Why did US walkout of UN Security Council meeting? Dispute with France, allegations against Human Rights Chief explained
local_articles.snippet: The US delegation on Monday exited a UN Security Council (UNSC) meeting in response to remarks made by France, which likened Washington's voting behavior on human rights to that of authoritarian regimes. {{^htLoading}} {{/htLoading}} This diplomatic dispute began the previous week when the US voted alongside North Korea and Russia against the extension of Volker Turk's tenure as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. questions.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Rule : Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-23 hydrologic escalation along the Danube flips the ranking sharply toward Romania and Hungary (Reuters, Libertatea/G4Media, ATV.hu, Power Trading News Europe): (1) Romania surges 0.27 -> 0.38 (new #1): Danube flow at Romania's entry plunged to 1,650-1,700 m3/s (lowest in 30 years since 1996 vs. 4,700 normal), forcing authorities to activate emergency irrigation restrictions on the Calarasi-Cernavoda stretch and execute controlled water releases from Olt and Arges reservoirs specifically to maintain minimum cooling flow for Cernavoda's two reactors; Apele Romane warned July 21 that recent rains failed to lift Danube flow, which is projected to stay near 1,700-1,750 m3/s through at least July 27, leaving Cernavoda (tight 15 cm gap between Unit 1/2 shutdown thresholds and 2003 shutdown precedent) acutely exposed. (2) Hungary climbs 0.20 -> 0.26 (new #2): BME nuclear engineering dean Attila Aszodi warned on ATV.hu (July 21) that the Danube at Paks fell 6 cm below its all-time record low (-104 cm Friday, -71 cm Tuesday), all three cooling parameters (temperature, level, flow) hit critical marks simultaneously, Paks was 'only a few cm' from a turbine shutdown and 25-30 cm from a complete plant shutdown, and 'we are not past the hardest part' (moderated slightly vs. Romania because Paks has 4 units with staged shutdown buffering). (3) Slovenia drops 0.36 -> 0.21 (#3): no mid/late-July Krsko cooling alerts, Krsko's auxiliary cooling towers held 100% power through June's heatwave, and Reuters (July 21) reported storms spreading directly into Slovenia—though single-reactor exposure keeps it a serious #3. Bulgaria (Kozloduy, 0.14 -> 0.13) faces the same record-low Danube (lowest since 1946 in Serbia) without reported cooling alerts yet; Belarus trims 0.02 -> 0.01 (sum 0.99).

local_articles.title: Jhoan Duran blows save as Miami Marlins snap 12-game skid in win over Philadelphia Phillies
local_articles.snippet: Griffin Conine hit a walkoff run-scoring single to lift the Marlins past the Philadelphia Phillies 8-7 on Monday and end Miami's franchise record 12-game losing streak. Phillies closer Jhoan Duran (1-4) entered with a 7-5 lead before loading the bases with no outs and allowing a tying two-run single by Heriberto Hernández, who scored the winning run. Hernández and Conine homered against Phillies ace Zack Wheeler. Jakob Marsee had a run-scoring double and Otto Lopez added an RBI triple for the Marlins, who hadn't won a game since July 9. The Phillies have struggled since the All-Star break, losing seven of 10. The Marlins built a 5-2 cushion in the first two innings against Wheeler before blowing it in the sixth and rallying in the ninth on Conine's first career walk-off hit and Miami's fifth walk-off win of the season.
